topic: Model routing across agents, pricing, advisor strategy

claims.claim: April 2026 Anthropic pricing: Opus 4.7 $5/$25 per M input/output tokens; Sonnet 4.6 $3/$15; Haiku 4.5 $1/$5.
Opus costs 5x Sonnet input and 5x Haiku input; 1.67x Sonnet output and 5x Haiku output. This asymmetry matters: output-heavy tasks suffer most from Opus-by-default.
GitHub Issue #27665 documents 93.8% of community-reported real Claude Code usage runs on Opus - indicates severe over-use of Opus for Haiku/Sonnet-appropriate tasks.
opusplan flag is currently broken/deprecated - the advertised 'Opus for plan, Sonnet for execution' pattern no longer works reliably as of April 2026.
--model opus sticks across the session: setting it once keeps Opus for everything including trivial Bash/Grep until explicitly reset.
Advisor strategy (explicit model per subagent, never inherit): Haiku for search/grep/extract/summarize; Sonnet for code edits; Opus for planning, synthesis, and conflict resolution.
claims.source: Community consensus + Anthropic multi-agent research system

claims.claim: Maciej's Deep Research v2 preset (internal case study) uses: Orchestrator Opus, Researchers Sonnet, Extractors Haiku, Critic+Syntetyk Opus; proven to cut Opus spend by ~60% vs all-Opus baseline.
Haiku 4.5 performance on extraction/summarization/grep-style tasks matches Sonnet 4.6 in benchmarks; model-quality is not the constraint for these tasks.
model frontmatter field in subagent definitions accepts specific IDs; setting this explicitly is the most reliable way to route work off Opus.
Inherit is the default when model is omitted; this is the primary mechanism by which Opus-by-default leaks to subagents.
Built-in Explore subagent uses Haiku; Plan uses inherit; this is why Explore is explicitly recommended for search/enumeration while Plan inherits for reasoning.
Prompt caching (90% discount on cached read) is effective for subagents if the system prompt + CLAUDE.md are identical across calls; cache hits can offset 5-10k tokens of entry tax.
Multi-agent systems consume ~15x more tokens than chat; justified only when outcome value is at least that much greater.
claims.source: Anthropic engineering blog multi-agent research system

claims.claim: Flags --premium / --budget / --ultra-budget in Deep Research v2 map to model tier overrides: premium = all-Opus, budget = Sonnet-heavy, ultra-budget = Haiku-heavy with Sonnet only for Critic.
Weekly rate limits on Max plan: ~10 hours of heavy Opus use hits weekly quota; explicit Haiku routing for extractors extends useful session time 3-5x.
For dev teams sharing a workspace, a CLAUDE.md directive 'default to Sonnet for implementation, Opus only for architecture' shifts routing without code changes.

conflicts_flagged.description: Anthropic docs and SDK examples default model: inherit, but community consensus says this is a footgun. Docs-vs-practice mismatch.
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Synthesis should call out: docs' default inheritance is the leading cause of Opus over-use; practitioners should override.

conflicts_flagged.description: opusplan was once the recommended approach; now deprecated/broken. Older tutorials still cite it.
conflicts_flagged.resolution_hint: Mark opusplan as stale; direct readers to explicit per-subagent model.

gaps_flagged.description: No official benchmark comparing Haiku 4.5 vs Sonnet 4.6 on agentic tool-use workloads; community evidence only.
No token-cost calculator published for multi-agent workflows; each team has to measure independently.
Interaction between prompt caching and dynamic CLAUDE.md updates unclear - cache invalidation rules not documented.
